systems.name: creative-apps
systems.description: The macOS app shells of the creative suite: five SwiftUI apps (Flare, Design, Photo, Library, Halo), each over a Linux-safe Model target, plus the SuiteUI design system.

containers.name: SuiteUI
containers.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): tokens, Liquid Glass primitives, the SuiteWindow shell, toolbar palette, sidebar rows and sections, content-layer surfaces, pro inspector rows and scrub fields, a thumbnail grid, a timeline strip and AppMark, the app marks. macOS only; knows no app Model or engine, only SuiteModel's app list.

components.name: SuiteUI sources
components.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI, linking SuiteModel for SuiteApp): spacing, radius, size, type and color tokens; Liquid Glass applied in one snapshot-aware place (Glass) and GlassPanel; the SuiteWindow shell (sidebar, content, inspector) with SidebarSection and SidebarRow; ToolbarGroup palette actions; the content layer (CanvasSurface, SurfaceCard, EmptyStateView, ViewerStatusBar, BusyNote for open, save and import progress, and TransportCapsule, the shared transport over TransportStepping); the editor-kernel chrome (SuiteExportSheet, SuiteStrokePacer, SuitePointerPressure, BrushCursorMark, and ToolKeys, the one tool-letter lookup and the one map from AppKit modifier flags to KeyModifiers); the editor shell after the Ripple editor (EditorShell, EditorTopBar and its bar items, the docked ToolbarGroup rail, CanvasViewport with its Ruler, optional checkerboard, ZoomMath clamped zoom and fit with SuiteCanvasNavigating, the live CanvasNavigating over it, SuiteHandleGeometry, the live HandleGeometryProviding over the kernel's BoxMath and HandleHit, and CanvasMarks with SelectionHandlesEditor, the selection box whose handles resize and rotate it, SegmentedTabs and the ColorWell hex row); pro inspector parts (InspectorHeader, InspectorRows, ScrubField and NumericInput number entry); the Studio easing parts (CurveEditor, StudioScrubRow, ChoiceChips); AppMark, the one view that draws an app's mark (icon, glyph or line style) from AppMarkArt, path data scripts/render-marks generates from Bundle/Marks; ThumbnailGrid with its selection math; and TimelineStrip with its frame mapping, shared by Flare and Halo, with TimelineLaneLayers, the rules of its AppKit lanes renderer (which lanes redraw from an Equatable diff, a layer frame per lane, a press routed to the lane classification).

containers.name: FlareApp
containers.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/FlareApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads FlareModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: FlareApp sources
components.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene, its menu bar (FlareCommands) and views in Sources/FlareApp, including the inspector's TIMING row (FlareInspectorTiming: the selected span's easing preset name) and the easing popover it opens (FlareEasingPopover: presets, the four bezier numbers and the curve) on the live FlareWorkspace, built from SuiteUI, and PlaybackDriver, which feeds NSScreen display-link target timestamps into the workspace's play clock, and StagePath, which turns FlareCore paths and colors into CGPath (one addCurve per cubic) and sRGB CGColor for the stage, and StageRasterizer, the PNG export rasterizer (LA-1): FrameRasterizing on a CoreGraphics RGBA8 sRGB bitmap that draws a StageDrawList at 1x or 2x exactly as the stage does, the background unless transparent, and encodes it through ImageIO, and FlareAutosave, which writes the dirty document's RecoveryFile atomically off the main actor once autosave is due and removes it after a save, and on launch reads and decodes it off the main thread into a RecoveryOffer to restore or discard, and FlareWindow, the SuiteWindow with the toolbar, sidebar and inspector that routes every control through one FlareIntent, and FlareToolItems (each FlareTool's palette title, symbol and one-key shortcut), the router (FlareWindow+Router and one FlareWindow+<area> file per FlareIntent area, each acting or giving the reason it can't), and the window's area views: FlareStage (the artboard drawn in a Canvas on CanvasViewport, its overlay of draft, marquee and selection outline drawn from the drag's FlareLiveDrag while one lasts, so the window's body runs once per drag, and the floating tool palette), FlareTimeline (one TimelineStrip lane per layer, ruler scrub and the timecode and frame readouts), FlareTransport (start, step, play/pause, end and loop; FlareCanvas runs PlaybackDriver while playing and the stage status bar shows the rate pills), FlareRecording (the auto-key recording ring), FlareFilePanels (the open, save and export folder panels, the title's dirty dot, and the save and open alerts), FlareExportSheetAdapter (the Model's export run on SuiteUI's export sheet; FlareWindow+Export runs the exporter off the main actor and writes its files all or nothing, never over an existing file), FlareInspector (Properties and Library tabs), FlarePasteboard (Cut, Copy and Paste carry the Model's layer bytes on NSPasteboard.general under the suite's SuiteTypeID.flareLayers, and a change-count watch keeps Edit > Paste current), FlareStageContextMenu (the stage's Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete, Bring Forward and Send Backward, each disabled with its reason) and the stubs later tasks fill (FlareLibraryPanel and the new sheet, open status and recovery modifiers).

containers.name: FlareModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window. FlareWorkspace: the open FlareCore document, selected scene and drawing tool. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: FlareModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window: FlareWorkspace (document, selection, tool, frame and playback, drafts) and FlareServices: the use-case contracts, their live conformances over FlareCore (LiveStage, LiveHits, LiveShapes, LiveProperties, LiveKeyframes, LiveEasing, LiveScenes, and LiveExportAdapter, FlareCore's SVG, Lottie and PNG exporters over any stage: text removed first, a cancel between PNG frames writes nothing, every result carries ExportScan's warnings), and the fixture fakes the UI track and snapshots run on. FlareLaunch parses the launch flags (-FlareFixture, -FlareSample, -FlareOpenFile, -FlareSaveTo) into the workspace's first document and services, and FlareServicesBuilt is FlareServices.built, the live type for every member whose live conformance has merged, which a launch without -FlareFixture runs on. FlareIntent names every control of the window as one case per area with a stable identifier, and FlareIntent+Titles gives each its menu or toolbar title. FlareStageRead gives the stage its draw list (the drag preview while a move runs) and marks (draft, marquee, selection bounds); FlareTimelineRead gives the timeline its rows, empty text and selected row; FlarePenFinish ends an open pen path on Return as one step. FlareWorkspaceState holds the export, assist and file-load states the workspace stores. FlareFiles opens .flare files through load (progress first, a pure decode the app runs off the main thread, then the landing), hands the app a save's bytes, and keeps the file name, the window title and the dirty flag (the document against the one last opened or saved), with section 3.3's alert text for each FormatError, the Open Recent list (file paths, most recent first, at most ten), and the autosave due time (30 seconds after the last edit, only while dirty) with the recovery bytes of the dirty document, and restoring a recovered document as unsaved, untitled work; FlareFiles+Kernel reads the dirty flag and the autosave verdict from SuiteKernel's DocumentSession, ends every coalescing run on a save, and gives the launch offer as the kernel's RecoveryOffer. FlareSelection picks layers or items by click, Shift-click and marquee, and gives the selection box's bounds; FlareDrag turns stage gestures into a draft or move preview and commits each once, on mouse-up, as one named undo step; FlareLiveDrag runs a drag's samples on a copy of the workspace the window doesn't observe, for the stage to draw until mouse-up hands the window the last one; FlareDrawing adds the Ellipse tool's draft and its one-step commit; FlareScenes adds, renames, removes (never the last), reorders and sets up scenes; FlareGuides adds, moves (one coalesced step per drag), removes and clears ruler guides; FlareEdit runs the Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Select All, Deselect), each one named undo step or disabled with the reason it refuses with; FlareAnimate holds auto-key and the inspector's animated properties (Mixed across layers, one coalesced step per scrub, the stopwatch and keyframe button); EasingEditing is the easing editor's contract, which FlareWorkspace conforms to over FlareCore's SetKeyframeEasing, with FakeEasingEditing as its in-memory stand-in for UI work. FlareOnionState holds onion skin and motion path preferences and reads ghosts and the path from services.onion. FlareServices holds one fake per use-case contract (FakeScenes, FakeStage, FakeHits, FakeShapes, FakeProperties with section 2's not-animated rule, FakeKeyframes, FakeEasing, FakeOnion, FakeLibrary, FakeMachines, FakePreview and FakeExport with FakeRasterizer so far, NotBuilt for the rest) over the fixture documents in FlareFixtures (empty, bounce, character, button, button with states, button with machine and showcase). ExportScan names everything an export can't write (text, symbol animation, machines, Lottie's background); FlareExport holds the export sheet's options, warnings and run. FlareSymbols holds the Library tab's symbols and swatches, Convert to Symbol, place, the reason Delete is disabled while a symbol is in use, and editing a symbol in place: the owner switch, the symbol's length on the timeline and the scene frame to return to. FlarePlaybackTicks is the playback driver's platform-neutral core: PlaybackTicker turns display-link target timestamps into the elapsed seconds the play clock advances by, FlareWorkspace.tick is the link's entry point, and PlaybackBudget holds QB-L4's dropped-frame gate. MachineLayout lays out a state machine's graph for the Interactions editor: columns by breadth-first distance from the initial state, unreachable states in a last column. FlareMachines holds the Interactions editor's state: the edited machine, states from frame labels, transitions and inputs, each edit one named undo step through services.machines with refusals in machineError, and the live preview over services.preview, which any machine edit stops. BoxGestureMath is the box move, scale and rotate math FakeShapes and LiveShapes share; its handles 0...7 are SuiteKernel's EditorHandle ring, numbered and placed by the kernel through BoxGestureMath+Kernel. FlareLayers+Kernel projects the edited owner's layers into SuiteKernel's LayerTree (FlareLayerPayload), whose front-to-back order and rows the Layers section reads, and runs each panel move through LayerTree.move before FlareCore's ReorderLayer. EasingEditing+Kernel and KeyframeEditing+Kernel put Flare's easing presets, curve, keys (.all for the summary key) and key and frame rules on SuiteKernel's Keys (EasePreset, EaseCurve, KeyRef, Segment, KeyRules). FlareDocumentCommands+Catalog gives every FlareCore command id in CommandRegistry.builtIn a SuiteKernel catalog spec over FlareWorkspace (kebab-case id, SchemaProbe's schema or a hand-written one for layer commands, available when its example runs on a copy, run through the engine as one undo step, read back by FlareCoreHistory), with CommandSchemaProviding schemas for FlareCore's payload enums.

containers.name: DesignApp
containers.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built on SuiteUI's SuiteWindow and EditorDetail. Reads DesignModel and sends it intents through DesignWindow; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule). Cut, Copy and Paste carry the Model's layer bytes on the system pasteboard (DesignPasteboardBridge).

components.name: DesignApp sources
components.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built on SuiteUI's SuiteWindow and EditorDetail: the window and its intents (DesignWindow, DesignIntent), the window toolbar's commands (DesignToolbarItem), the floating tool palette, the canvas (DesignArtwork with its text drawn by DesignTextArtwork, then an overlay above the page clip with the layers past the page edge dimmed outside it in DesignPastEdge, the frame names in DesignFrameLabels, the selection marks and handles in DesignSelectionMarks, the marquee mark, and the tool feedback in DesignCanvasFeedback: the hover outline, the Text tool's dashed placement box and the live size badge) and the inline text editor at canvas scale, both in each text layer's own family, size, weight and alignment from DesignTextFont, the sidebar (a List of the pages and the layer tree, whose rows rename in place and drag to reorder or nest behind an insertion line the panel holds), the Properties inspector (one layer, several layers with their shared or Mixed values, its Align and Distribute row in DesignAlignBar, its style rows in DesignInspectorStyle (Opacity, Corners, Stroke, the hint in the value column, and the frame fields, each scrub previewed on the live box), the Text section in DesignInspectorText (font family, size, weight and alignment, disabled on a layer that isn't text) and a page's Width and Height scrub fields in DesignInspectorPage), the File, Edit (Duplicate after the system's pasteboard items, in DesignEditMenu), Page (Add, Rename and Delete Page), Object (Group, Ungroup, the Arrange and Align submenus and Distribute, in DesignObjectMenu) and View (zoom, Zoom to Selection) menus, each Design item off with its Model help as its tooltip, the open and save panels, DesignRasterizer (the PNG of the Model's DesignRaster of an export item, drawn by DesignArtwork through ImageRenderer off the window and written as sRGB with alpha through ImageIO), and DesignLiveDrag, the window's live drag box: a canvas drag's samples and a scrub's values go to a copy only the canvas and the inspector's style rows draw, and land in the workspace as one step at the end.

containers.name: DesignModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: pages, the node tree on each page (with fills and text) and which Layers rows are expanded, the selection, the tool, the model-owned undo history, the canvas gestures and the file codec. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: DesignModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: DesignWorkspace (pages, the selected page and node, the tool, the open file's URL), the multi-layer selection (DesignSelection: the ordered selected layers with the last as primary, Shift-click toggling, the box around them), DesignNode (the node tree on a page, each node with a fill and text, in absolute page points) and the tree flattened into rows under the expanded set, DesignHistory (the model-owned undo and redo, one named step per edit; New File's step carries the replaced document's file URL, which Undo puts back), the canvas gestures (hit testing, the handles a selection shows, draw, move, resize, nudge, delete, in DesignCanvasEditing and DesignDrawing), what the canvas shows before a click (DesignCanvasHints: the hover answer, the Text tool's placement box, the size badge and where it hangs), what an arrow, Delete, Escape or Return pressed on the canvas does, ignoring the numeric-pad flag every arrow carries (DesignCanvasKeys), the inline text edit, whose commit fits the box to the measured text in the same step (DesignText), where the canvas puts a frame's name, above the frame or inside it at the artboard's top (DesignFrameLabel), the inspector's header lines (DesignInspectorContent), the lock that covers a node's subtree and the line saying why (DesignLocking), the Layers row's eye and lock toggles, the hidden-in-tree check and the move target a drop above, below or into a row maps to and the insertion line a pointer over a row draws (DesignLayerToggles), the held-id index id minting reads (DesignHeldIDs), aligning the selected layer to its enclosing frame or page with the reason a command is off (DesignAlign), the window toolbar's eight commands with their titles, symbols, identifiers and the reason each can't run (DesignToolbarItems), the page's size as one undo step, its visible content bounds and which layers reach past its edge (DesignPageSize), the file codec (DesignFile), the open document as SuiteKernel's DocumentSession over the history's step serials, a save setting its saved token and ending the edit run, and the file version read through VersionedJSON.probe (DesignSession+Kernel), the export contract (DesignExport+Kernel: the scope and options, the workspace's export targets, plan and SVG readouts over the export slot, and the remembered options, never a history step) and the SVG text of nodes inside a box (Live/DesignSVG), what a PNG of a planned export item draws (DesignRaster: the item's nodes moved to the origin on a page its whole-point size, the plan's pixel size and scale, a side over its max refused), the layer tree adapter onto SuiteKernel's LayerTree (DesignNode+Kernel: a node as the kernel's layer payload and back; Live/LiveOrdering's Move Layer and Arrange run on it and map its refusals to Design's by layer name), and the use cases a workspace runs on (DesignServices, whose `.live` set is NotBuilt in every slot until each feature lands: each help says the feature isn't built yet and each write refuses; `.fake` is the fixture fakes in Fakes/ that snapshots and fake-mode journeys use), and the workspace actions the window, menus and canvas call (DesignActions: each command's help and run through the services as one named undo step, one-layer delete, nudge and align on today's methods, Zoom to Selection and Select All; DesignActions+Edit: Copy, Cut and Paste, with Paste into the selected frame, Move Layer, and the inspector's style rows as DesignStyleChange, one-layer frame, fill and corner radius on today's methods), the command catalog (DesignCommandCatalog: every DesignCommand, palette tool, page and file action as a SuiteKernel CommandSpec whose availability is today's help and whose run is today's method, under ids kept in Tests/command-ids/design.txt), and DesignLiveEdit: the copy a canvas drag or inspector scrub shows until it ends, then replays into the workspace as one step.

containers.name: PhotoApp
containers.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads PhotoModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: PhotoApp sources
components.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI's SuiteWindow: the window and its intents, the window toolbar (Open, Save and Export beside the title, Undo, Redo and zoom trailing) with the save status as its subtitle, the layer list in the sidebar, the canvas under a floating tool palette with the status line beneath it, the inspector with no tabs (an image header, tool options, the selected layer's blend settings, and adjustment sections with the Levels gamma ScrubField and the Curves tone curve over its histogram), the export, image size and straighten sheets (the straighten preview turns the canvas picture on the GPU under a grid), the File, Edit (Undo, Redo, and Cut, Copy and Paste on the image unless a text field has focus or a sheet is up), Select, Image, Layer and View menus, the general pasteboard read and written as PNG and TIFF (PhotoPasteboard) and watched for the Edit menu, the coalescing canvas renderer, the stroke pacer that applies a display frame's drag samples at once, the pen pressure and the Option key read from AppKit for canvas drags, the window's autosave to a recovery file and its restore offer at launch (PhotoAutosave), the app delegate (Finder opens, and the unsaved-changes prompt on Quit) and the window's close guard that asks before a dirty window closes, and the ImageIO codec behind PhotoModel's PhotoImageCodec.

containers.name: PhotoModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: the canvas as a CoreRaster PixelBuffer, its layer stack, selected layer and tool, adjustment settings, and inspector and Layer menu state; the free transform's handle hit and drag math adapt onto SuiteKernel (LiveTransform+Kernel); the canvas picture renders through CoreRender's dispatcher on a PhotoRenderRoute. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: PhotoModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window, each menu, toolbar and palette action also a SuiteKernel catalog command (PhotoCommandCatalog: ids, availability from today's help, menu labels), PhotoHeadless (the window-less document the CLI and real jobs drive: open .ora, PNG and JPEG, save .ora, export PNG or JPEG at an optional long side, the catalog lifted onto it) over CoreRasterImageCodec (PNG and JPEG through creative-core, with a small own 8-bit PNG reader and writer until core's lands):PhotoWorkspace (the open image's size and name, the layer stack with each layer's offset and its pixels as copy-on-write CoreRaster tiles (TiledPixels), so an edit copies only the tiles it touches, the selected layer, tool, and the brush's and eraser's own tool options with the brush cursor diameter, the marquee selection and pending crop), the tools' drags (brush and eraser strokes and clone dabs sampled through SuiteKernel's stroke model, StrokeSmoother and DabSpacer, with each tool's options kept as kernel BrushSettings and a list of BrushPresets; marquee, crop, move, and the Clone and Heal tools' Option-click to sample and drag to clone or heal), the clone stamp (a sampled source and a stroke that copies from it at a fixed offset onto the selected layer, and heal, the same stroke with each dab shifted to the tone where it lands), selection edits and crop, Image Size, Rotate and Straighten (worked out off the main actor, committed unless the image changed), the undo history (the tiles an edit changed, layer lists and whole stacks, read as a list of named steps from "New Image" or "Open" with a jump to any step), the tile-parallel renderer with damage tracking (a full frame as the reference, or the live canvas's update: only the damaged tiles, premultiplied) and the adjustments it applies (exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, blur) with the curve editor's samples and histogram, opening and exporting through the PhotoImageCodec protocol, the adjustment settings and logarithmic gamma track (with the Gamma field's commit, a no-op for the value it shows), what the inspector shows (with the image header lines and the viewer status size text), and when each Layer menu item can run (with Bring Forward and Send Backward, one place up or down the stack, and Select Layer Above and Below), the layer stack's reorder, arrange, duplicate and show/hide run on SuiteKernel's LayerTree (a single-level tree of PhotoLayer payloads, bottom first, projected to and from the top-first list), and the live edit services (the clipboard and layer merging, through the renderer's per-layer composite) behind Cut, Copy and Paste of pixels (a pasted layer, or a new image with none open) and Duplicate Layer, Merge Down and Flatten Image, each one named undo step with its reason when it can't run.

containers.name: LibraryApp
containers.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads LibraryModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: LibraryApp sources
components.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI: the window with its thumbnail grid, the loupe (one photo on CanvasViewport at its own pixel size, its render or a placeholder, with its position readout, arrow keys and Escape), the inspector (one InspectorHeader above its Info and Develop tabs, library.inspector.header: the catalog's inspectorHeader, the collection's name and photo count with nothing selected, one photo's name, Captured, Size and Kind, or several photos' count and capture span) and its metadata inspector for the selected photos (rating, flag, color label), and the File > Load Sample Photos, View > Grid and Loupe, View > Sort By and thumbnail size commands, and the loupe area (View > Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom to Fit and Actual Size, Home and End, renders through a latest-wins RenderQueue on the loupe service, and the neighbours prefetched), and the thumbnails area, whose LibraryThumbnailStore holds the grid's images apart from the catalog so a thumbnail pass reruns the grid and not the window's body, and the status row under the grid and the loupe (LibraryStatusBar: the catalog's statusRow through ViewerStatusBar, its count or pixel size, selection, cell size, Fit and place, import, render, save and Preview data pills, each library.status.<id> with its help; no row on an empty live catalog).

containers.name: LibraryModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: the catalog's photos, sidebar collections with counts, the selected collection and sort order, and seeded sample photos. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: LibraryModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: LibraryCatalog (photos, collections with counts, the selected collection, sort order, the loupe's photo, stepping and position), PhotoItem with its sort orders, metadata edits on the selected photos with mixed values (PhotoMetadata, PhotoFlag) and the metadata inspector's accessibility identifiers (MetadataInspectorID), 60 seeded sample photos, and LibraryThumbnailCache (the grid's held thumbnails, pending requests and size bucket, reading the catalog without changing it and returning failures as availability changes for applyThumbnailFailures), and the status contract (LibraryStatusRow and LibraryStatusPill: the row under the content with its count, selection, cell size or loupe zoom and place, import, render, save and Preview data pills; LibraryInspectorHeader: the inspector's title and facts), and the export contract: export names (ExportNaming+Kernel, an adapter onto SuiteModel's UniqueFileNames) and the Library-local export formats, presets and XMP sidecar (ExportFormats, ExportPresets, ExportSidecar) with the catalog's export methods and runner (LibraryExport), and the menu and key actions (LibraryAction with the catalog's help and run, refusing with the menu's reason as a LibraryRefusal: LibraryActions).

containers.name: HaloApp
containers.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads HaloModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: HaloApp sources
components.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI: the window, the Layer and Composition menus, the composition inspector (Pro density header, Composition rows and layer list), the viewer's status bar and timeline strip (scrub, select a layer, I and O set in and out points), the New Composition sheet, the alert for a refused rename, and the hidden readouts the UI journeys read where XCUITest reads a value empty (#262).

containers.name: HaloModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: the project's compositions and their layers, the selected composition, New Composition settings, and refused renames. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: HaloModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: HaloProject (compositions, the selected one, unique names), HaloTimeline (each composition's playhead, timecodes, the layers active at a frame, the strip's rows, in and out points at the playhead), HaloLayer (kind, span, color, opacity, CoreRaster blend mode, solid rectangle), FrameRenderer (composites a composition's solids into one preview frame with CoreRaster), HaloStatusText (the inspector header, Composition rows and status-bar timecode text), the New Composition draft and its validated settings, RefusedRename, which keeps a refused composition rename for the alert, and the inspector TEXT section's rules (HaloTextDraft, a field draft kept with its layer; the refusals TEXT owns; the size bar's drag range), and the adapter onto SuiteKernel's Keys (HaloEasing+Kernel: HaloKeyRef, HaloKeySegment, HaloEasingPreset and HaloKeyState map to KeyRef, Segment, EasePreset and KeyState; handles and key rules run on EaseCurve and KeyRules), and the adapter onto SuiteKernel's LayerTree (HaloLayers+Kernel: a composition's layers as a single-level tree whose follow link is each layer's parentID; moves, bring/send, duplicate, world placement and the parent picker run on it).

containers.name: SuiteModel
containers.description: Linux-safe values, contracts, fakes and pure logic shared by every app and the launcher. Foundation only; imports no app Model and no engine.

components.name: Identity and type registry
components.description: SuiteApp (the five apps and the launcher), bundle ids under one prefix (SuiteIdentity.prefix), and SuiteTypeRegistry: every document and pasteboard type each app reads and writes and the default app per type. Bundle/Info/*.plist mirror it; a test checks both. UniqueFileNames: the one unique-file-name rule every app's export uses ("Card.png", then "Card 2.png"). XMLText: the one XML text and attribute escaper every export writer uses (Design's SVG, Photo's stack.xml).

components.name: Suite store
components.description: SuiteLocations (the support folder, -SuiteSupportDir override) and FileStore: revisioned JSON files written by atomic replace under an exclusive lock file, merged with the caller's pure merge.

components.name: Contracts
components.description: One protocol per suite use case (blueprint section 5): switching, recents, new documents, routing, hand-offs, round trip, pasteboard, assets, links, animation import, preferences, settings route, onboarding, updates, thumbnails, home, and SuiteDocumentHost, which each app Model conforms to so it can act on hand-offs.

components.name: Fakes and fixtures
components.description: A fake per contract with an unavailable reason, and SuiteFixtures: the journeys' store contents, written into the live store by the launcher.

components.name: Services
components.description: SuiteServices: one member per contract, .fake and the slots SuiteShell fills for .live.

components.name: Recents
components.description: RecentsList: merge, dedupe by file identity, cap 200, filter by app, search; the rules for when an app records.

components.name: Routing
components.description: Which app opens a type, the Open In list for a document, and Finder routing decisions for the launcher.

components.name: Hand-offs
components.description: HandOff values (verb, payload, return address), the versioned codec and the lifecycle (pending, accepted, returned, cancelled, expired).

components.name: Switching
components.description: Switch requests and receipts, run states, the Switch To menu model.

components.name: Home state
components.description: Home sections (new tiles and presets, recents grid, running apps strip), search and filter, HomeLayout column math, and HomeModel, the home window's observable view-model.

components.name: Pasteboard coding
components.description: SuiteClipItem and its typed representations (suite asset envelope, SVG, PNG, colour, text); best-item choice for a target app.

components.name: Round trip
components.description: Library to Photo to Library edit sessions and their states.

components.name: Assets
components.description: SuiteAsset, SuiteSwatch, the asset index: add, update with a new revision, remove, search.

components.name: Links
components.description: AssetLink and its status (current, update available, missing) for placed assets.

components.name: Animation import
components.description: AnimationSummary of a .flare file (size, rate, length, scenes) for Halo's Open In.

components.name: Preferences
components.description: StorePreferences, the live PreferencesStoring over FileStore's preferences.json: load with the store's revision, save with the stale check and revision + 1, changes() and externalChange().

components.name: Onboarding
components.description: SuiteOnboarding (the live OnboardingFlowing: pages, show-once-per-version, focus to home order), OnboardingLaunch (the first-launch rule and the -SuiteSkipOnboarding flag), SampleCatalog (one sample per app, its folder, copy destination and ref), OnboardingStarter and the control ids, and OnboardingModel (the welcome window's view-model).

components.name: Updates
components.description: Update feed parsing, version comparison, the offer and the install plan.

components.name: AI access

The modules under Sources/SuiteKernel/<Module>/ are their own parts.

EK-2 declares it as a stub that keeps its ids; EK-10 fills the bodies and adds Nudge and Marquee here.

components.name: Keys and easing

Keys/KeyRules.swift: KeyRules (key state, toggle a key or the animation, move keys all or nothing in a range, remove by policy, insert and remove frames) and KeyRefusal. Stubs from EK-3; bodies EK-15 and EK-16.
components.technology: Swift 6, Foundation (FoundationEssentials) and FlareCore, Linux and macOS

components.name: Layer tree and fixtures
components.description: LayerTree<Payload>, the one layer tree: LayerPayload, LayerNode (nesting, hide, lock, a follow link), LayerRow (the layers panel's flat rows from rows(expanded:)), ArrangeStep and TreeRefusal; move, arrange, group, ungroup, duplicate and the follow link are stubs for EK-12 and EK-13. Fakes/KernelFixtures.swift holds the shared fixtures: tree200 (200 nodes, seven roots, groups three deep, one hidden, one locked) and cards (the snapping packet's page in Desktop). Fakes/FakeCanvasDocument.swift is the command catalog's fake app: a headless document of named rects with its six commands plus undo and redo, its fixture, and CommandCatalog.empty for an app that has adopted no command yet.

components.technology: Swift 6, Foundation (FoundationEssentials) and FlareCore, Linux and macOS

components.name: Box transform and handle hit

Transform/HandleHit.swift: HandleHit (the handle under a point, Chebyshev with corners winning ties; a screen tolerance divided by zoom). Stubs from EK-3; bodies EK-20.
components.technology: Swift 6, Foundation (FoundationEssentials) and FlareCore, Linux and macOS

components.name: Export run and document session

Session/DocumentSession.swift: SaveStatus, DocumentSession (dirty from the saved and current tokens, autosave due a delay after the last edit, didSave and didEdit, stateText: the save indicator word every app shows), UnsavedPrompt (the one unsaved-changes alert wording and Save / Don't Save / Cancel choices every app builds) and RecoveryOffer. Session/VersionedJSON.swift: VersionedJSON (probe a file's version before decoding, a decoding error in words) and VersionError. Stubs from EK-3; bodies EK-22 and EK-24.

components.name: Stroke
components.description: Stroke/: StrokeSample (point, pressure, time) and the strokeSamples fixture (40 samples), StrokeSegment (a cubic with a pressure range), StrokeSmoother (samples to segments one late, flattening), DabSpacer (dab centres between two points), BrushSettings with BrushEdit (size, hardness, opacity, flow, spacing, clamped), BrushPreset, and LiveCopy, the working copy a drag draws on until take(). EK-29 declares them as stubs; EK-28 fills the bodies.
components.technology: Swift 6, Foundation (FoundationEssentials) and FlareCore, Linux and macOS

Reads the target's HistoryReading; never owns a history.

containers.name: afterglow CLI
containers.description: The headless `afterglow` command line tool: drives every app's command catalog on files with no window (`afterglow <app> <command> --json '{…}'`, open, export, list-commands, describe) and runs `*.jobs.json` scripts over sets of input files, which are also the real-jobs suites. One JSON object on stdout per run, sysexits exit codes. AfterGlowCLICore holds the router and every route, testable in process; AfterGlowCLI is the thin executable (product `afterglow`). Builds and runs on Linux, so cloud leads and CI drive the apps through it (docs/blueprints/suite/features/afterglow-cli.md).

components.name: CLI runner
components.description: The `afterglow` executable (AfterGlowCLI/main.swift: hands the arguments and LiveIO, the real disk with stdout and stderr, to CLI.run and exits with its code; CLIBinaryTests spawns it to check it agrees with CLI.run in process) and the router in AfterGlowCLICore: CLI.run, CLI.version and the sysexits codes (CLI.Exit), with the parser, output, file system and app registry files the single-shot forms use. CLIIO is everything the CLI touches outside itself (files, globs, stdout, stderr), with FakeIO, the tests' in-memory file system, and LiveIO, the real one (regular files only, a 2 GiB read cap, writes that make missing folders, then land a temp file by rename or by a hard link that refuses an existing target, globs walked without a shell); Apps is the registry, each app's HeadlessDocument erased to a HeadlessApp (photo, design, flare, halo, library, plus the fake for tests) whose HeadlessSession runs, saves and exports one open document. CL-1 makes `--version` live (one JSON object, sorted keys, exit 0); every other form exits 69 naming the slice that builds it until CL-4 fills them.

components.name: CLI batch runner
components.description: `afterglow run <script.jobs.json>`: ScriptRunner, which runs a versioned list of command steps over a set of input files and writes each output by name template, and Script, the format's Codable shape and validation. CL-7 fills it over the catalog's runBatch: validate the whole script (version 1, a known app, every step id and the output format), expand the inputs in sorted order, plan every output and refuse collisions (73) before anything is written, run each input all or none when atomic, and print one report; files are reached only through CLIIO.

components.name: Real-jobs harness
components.description: RealJobs: runs a `Tests/RealJobs/<app>/<job>/` script through the batch runner (ScriptRunner, its report captured) and compares each expected output: sha256 on the whole digest (a pure-Swift SHA-256, FIPS 180-4), JSON parsed and compared equal, or pixels within a tolerance in 255ths. A job whose platforms leave this one out is skipped before it runs with "macOS-only: <why>"; a pixel expectation is skipped "waits on image-codecs" until creative-core can decode PNG, never passed. Prints one JSON report: ok, or the failing paths and why, or skipped and its reason.

components.name: MCP server
components.description: `afterglow mcp`: a Model Context Protocol server over stdio that serves every app's command catalog as tools. MCPVersions pins the protocol revisions (2026-07-28 sessionless; 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 start with initialize); JSONRPC frames one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per line; MCPServer (with MCPOptions: apps, roots, limits) answers each line; MCPTools lists the tools and routes a tool name to an MCPRoute; MCPSessions holds the open documents by expiring handle and returns MCPToolResults. afterglow-mcp MC-1 declares them as stubs (serve still exits 69); MC-4, MC-6 and MC-8 fill the server, the tools and the calls.
